reviewer: Kimi independent actual visual comparison of the exact 65x67 source PNG, enlarged existing source-page 09 and targeted source panel crop, complete unchanged 2048x2048 raw RGBA and native-resolution face/frame/note crop, full white/cyan/alpha review sheet and unchanged naiwa.png; checked grey hair, brows, wire spectacles, absence of facial hair, one mouth, uniform/collar/cross, pose, crop, lighting, collar fit, and the original frame/note/backplate versus added hardware plus visible transparency.

remaining_reasons: The returned native pixels add TWO conspicuous circular metallic pins/studs that are absent from the enlarged original: one on the upper-left dark photo-frame rail and one near the upper center of the cream note. Remove both invented hardware objects and restore the source's plain frame and paper surfaces; do not substitute other new fasteners or marks while preserving the complete original frame, note and opaque backing.
entries.positive_observation: Short light-grey hair brushed back from a high mildly receding hairline, cropped sides, short grey sideburns, thin grey eyebrows and fine wire-rim spectacles remain. The jaw and chin are smooth without a moustache or beard, and there is one serious closed mouth. The three-quarter pose faces and gazes viewer left with a slight forward inclination, chest-up crop and soft frontal modeling. The dark olive uniform retains gold shoulder detailing, red collar patches with pale/gold trim and one dark-centered silver-white cross at the throat. The rounded chin meets a short broad fitted collar without a stalk, pinching or clipping. The underlying complete tilted frame, opaque pale warm-grey photographic backplate, overlapping cream note with upper marks and mostly blank lower paper, and small right-edge tab remain. Full white/cyan comparisons show no visible interior holes, lost backing or working-matte outer ring; the two added pins are the separate visible rejection reason above.
entries.visible_limitations: Fine spectacle rims, collar embroidery and note lettering cannot be read reliably at 65x67 and are not rejection grounds. The rejection is instead based on two clearly resolved native-output metal circles whose absence is also clear on the enlarged source frame and note; no microscopic inference is needed.
